subject.title: [Bug]: Config validator rejects mediaLocalRoots despite type definitions supporting it (Telegram outbound)

question: Should OpenClaw expose configurable outbound local media roots, and should the canonical surface be broad `tools.fs.roots`, a narrow media/channel key, or managed staging only?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes which host paths Telegram/channel delivery can read and upload, so automation should not choose the permanent security and product boundary.

options.title: Use One Canonical Root Policy
options.body: Settle a shared filesystem/media-root contract first, then implement one schema/runtime/docs/test path that covers Telegram and sibling media surfaces.

options.title: Add A Narrow Telegram Key
options.body: Expose `channels.telegram.mediaLocalRoots` for Telegram outbound media only, accepting the risk that it may later need consolidation with broader media-root policy.

options.title: Keep Managed Roots Only
options.body: Decline new host-root config for now and document managed media/workspace staging as the supported security boundary.

recommendation.title: Use One Canonical Root Policy
recommendation.body: Settle a shared filesystem/media-root contract first, then implement one schema/runtime/docs/test path that covers Telegram and sibling media surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest sampled history across outbound media policy, default local media roots, and the gateway/config paths that would define the boundary.
